findings.issue: The plan says to use `StynxError` without `context` for the two conflict codes, but STYNX has two classes with that name. `packages/contracts/src/errors.ts` has `StynxError(message, code, details)`, which has no `status`. `packages/core/src/errors.ts` has `StynxError(message, {code,status,...})`. `StynxErrorFilter` (`packages/core/src/error.filter.ts`) only recognizes the core class and rethrows anything else, so throwing the contracts class would give a 500, not a 400. That filter also translates the message by `messageKey` (which defaults to `code`) when an `STYNX_ERROR_TRANSLATOR` is registered and a locale is active, so the pinned message text only holds when no translator is registered. `packages/backend/package.json` does not depend on `@stynx-nyx/core`, so the conflict cannot be thrown from `AuthContextGuard` without editing that package's manifest.
findings.required_change: In the Architect contract (and in `01-ctg-0001-architect.md` when the exception class is pinned), name `@stynx-nyx/core` `StynxError` with `status: 400` and no `context`. State that the tenancy package raises both conflicts. State that the literal message holds when no `STYNX_ERROR_TRANSLATOR` is registered. The Inspector's exact status and body assertions already catch a mistake here, so this does not block dispatch.

findings.issue: The contract requires an app that uses `@PublicTenantRoute` without `StynxTenancyModule` to fail at initialization, but it does not say which module runs that check. The check must also work in apps that use only backend `AuthContextGuard`. `packages/backend/package.json` depends only on `contracts`, `idempotency` and `ratelimit`, not on `auth`, `core` or `tenancy`. So a check placed only in tenancy or core never runs in the app that is missing the module.
findings.required_change: Have the Architect define a public-tenant options token in `contracts`. Name the bootstrap check in `auth` or `core`, and in `backend`, that finds the marker's metadata and fails when the token is missing. Do this without adding package dependencies, because manifest edits would require a lockfile change.

summary: All eight items from review 2 are resolved, including the blocker. (1) UUID: `actorId` must be a valid RFC UUID (v4 or v7), validated at module init. PostgreSQL's `::uuid` cast (`0008_audit.sql:295`, `0017:21`, `0014_flow.sql:600`, `0018_worklist.sql:236`) accepts any valid UUID, and audit `actor_id` has no foreign key to `auth.users`, so the constraint is sufficient. The Inspector adds a boot-time rejection test and a real-PostgreSQL audited write under tenant A's RLS. (2) Route marker and RBAC tooling: `@PublicTenantRoute` composes `STYNX_PUBLIC_ROUTE`, and both guards check its metadata before their generic public early return (`stynx-auth.guard.ts:35`). `scripts/list-routes.mjs:354` and `verify-api-coverage.mjs:379` are assigned to the Engineer and `INV-RBAC-001` to the Architect. (3) Module ownership is `StynxTenancyModule.forRoot({publicTenant})`; `forRoot` already exists. `AuthContextGuard` defers its hard-coded `x-tenant-id` resolver to tenancy on public tenant routes. (4) Optional authentication: a valid token without membership gets 403 with no downgrade to the public actor, and the legacy unverified-claim path on plain `@Public()` routes is explicitly out of scope. (5) Exact bodies: they match the filter's passthrough of `HttpException` bodies and the current messages in `tenant-context.interceptor.ts:83-103`. (6) Only Express support is claimed. (7) `record.md` shows the green baseline. (8) The SSE-06/AUTHZ-07 dependency is recorded for CTG-2. UPS-TEN-01…06 map to the contract and tests: order under option (b), Host×header rejection per OD-S15-01, 400 for a missing tenant, `TenantResolverContext.host`/`path`, preserved legacy behavior plus the `rls-negative` and `rls-smoke` checks, and the migration note via changeset rather than the Angular-only `MIGRATING.md`. The three spec §3 negatives are covered, and §8 still has no addenda. Role-by-path follows Constitution Art. 6 (`law/`, `docs/` → Architect; `packages/` and scripts → Engineer; tests → Inspector). The sequence is complete: Architect `law/` commit → Inspector → Architect trace rebind → Engineer → maestro baselines, READMEs and gates. The remaining findings are implementation details that the Architect can settle and the Inspector's tests will catch, so dispatch is safe.
